name: Enets, Forest
confidence_why: Tereshchenko 1993, repeated in Siegl 2013, puts word stress predominantly on the first syllable, and Khanina 2018 agrees the first syllable is the prominent one more often than not but finds no clearly fixed stress, with the second syllable also often prominent, so the initial placement is secure while the strictness of the rule is not.
catalog_quote: Словесное ударение падает преимущественно на первый слог. Гласные в ударной позиции имеют относительно большую длительность, чем в неударной.
readall_conflicts: The one listed work (Siegl 2011, open copy) is silent, so nothing here contradicts the catalog's StressTyp2 initial-stress record. However, three Enets works already held by the project in the same check folder from the 2026-09-16 pass (not in this task's works list) hedge the 'fixed initial' reading and should be weighed when the site entry is. Khanina 2018 ( lines 191-205, printed p. 433, sec. 1.4, on Enets = Forest and Tundra together): 'As is typical for Uralic languages, the first syllable is often more prominent in Enets than other syllables: all three stress-related parameters (length, intensity, and pitch) can contribute to prominence. The second syllable can also be prominent; further syllables are rarely prominent, though there are some exceptions connected to some affixes that tend to be prominent.. In short, the situation with Enets stress is very messy and a proper study of stress in Enets is yet to be undertaken. For the moment, it is only clear that there is no easily identifiable fixed stress in Enets, and that the first syllable is more prominent than other syllables more often than not.' Khanina & Shluinsky 2022 (the text layeroffprint p. 5, sec. 2.2): 'Phonetic realization of stress does not display any distinctions in the two Enets either.' audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (initial), not in the strict set; keep rule 10/100/1000.. as the dominant pattern, keep Siegl's odd-syllable secondary stress in the primary-stress rule, add caution citing Khanina 2018:433 ('no easily identifiable fixed stress.. first syllable is more prominent.. more often than not; second syllable can also be prominent') and Tereshchenko 1993:345 'преимущественно' / 1966:441 'чаще всего' with her non-initial minimal pairs. Rationale: of four primary statements held, only Siegl 2013 says 'fixed'; the two Tereshchenko sketches hedge and the newest phonology article denies fixedness while agreeing initial is dominant. If the editor prefers to keep fixed-strict on Siegl's consultant re-test, the minimum action is a caution/contra entry for Khanina 2018.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations confirmed verbatim in copies we hold (Siegl 2013 p.102 in the fore1265 morph dir; Tereshchenko 1993 p.345 and 1966 p.441 in the tund1254 our files). (2) Deciding source is the 523-pp 2013 reference grammar, the best comprehensive description, but its stress section is a single impressionistic paragraph. (3) The Glottolog-listed phonology article Khanina 2018 (not previously. downloaded now with two open 2022 Helsinki Festschrift papers, all saved with a script-stamped under explicitly states there is no easily identifiable fixed stress in Enets, first syllable most often prominent, second syllable sometimes prominent, and that no proper stress study exists; Pleshak 2022 confirms the absence of prosodic work. No instrumental word-stress study was found. (4) Hence the initial location is we

sources.quote: Second-hand on word stress: 'there has been almost no work done on Enets prosody so far'; cites Khanina (2018:433) that 'the most prominent syllable is the first one' and 'there is no lexical stress in Enets that would be easily identifiable', and Tereshchenko (1966:441) that 'every odd syllable in an Enets word is prominent'; characterises Enets word-level prosody as 'based on the rhythm, rather than logical prominence'. Pilot phrasal-intonation study, not a word-stress study.
